subject: blavFitIndices Error: effective number of parameters exceeds the number of sample statistics

messages.author: ade7e6cb60aa84f9
messages.subject: blavFitIndices Error: effective number of parameters exceeds the number of sample statistics
parts:
Hello fellow blavaan users,
I estimated SEMs with the same structure for different indicators (RTs, Accuracies, Drift Rates from Diffusion model) and for some models I get an error when calculating the Bayesian Fit Measures telling me that the number of parameters exceed the number of sample statistics. For others the Fit Indices are calculated just fine and are in a reasonable range.

I have checked with maximum likelihood estimation and all SEM for all indicators are identified. Anything else would be surprising given that they use the same number of indicators with the same model structure.
I suspect that this might be a problem with the devM calculation, because for the models that throw the error I get the warning:  sqrt(nonc/(dif.ppD * N)) : NaNs produced. This seems to mean that either the non-centrality value is smaller than zero, or the dif.ppD gets negative.

Has someone encountered this error before and can help with resolving this?
Thanks for your help.
Cheers, Gidon

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: blavFitIndices Error: effective number of parameters exceeds the number of sample statistics
parts:
Gidon,

I believe that is a warning instead of an error. So it is informing you that effective number of parameters is larger than a traditional parameter count, which may cause problems for some model summaries, but the software doesn't know for sure. It would be helpful to see the code for your model, as well as the fitMeasures() output for your model.

Ed

I fixed the loadings, because all latent factors only have two indicators and then freely estimating the loadings results in locally unidentified measurement models. messages.subject: Re: blavFitIndices Error: effective number of parameters exceeds the number of sample statistics
parts:
Gidon

The issue is that ths discrepancy in number of parameters and small models lead to negative or equal to 0 values in th formula for RMSEA.

On the issue of "local identification", it is recommended to have locally identified factors but is not a requirement. There is a debate if it is actually neccesary or not. I prefer it but there is not strong research in favor of one. Also, you can locally identify them without fixing them to 1, can equate the factor loadings, this way you would have only one estimated factor loading, and would be with std.lv=T , with a fix variance method of identification (which I prefer and recommend)

gPerf =~ l1*CD + l1*DE
